categories.name: ensemble_composition
categories.definition: Adding, removing, swapping, or selecting which distinct models or model families are included as members of an ensemble.
examples: Add a diverse backbone to the ensemble
adding a new ensemble member from a different framework or training pipeline

categories.name: ensemble_blend_weights
categories.definition: Tuning, searching, or selecting the numeric weights or averaging scheme used to combine ensemble member predictions.

categories.name: ensemble_averaging_strategy
categories.definition: Choosing the method or mathematical form of combining predictions across ensemble members (e.g., rank-based vs probability-based, uniform vs weighted).
examples: uniform averaging of diverse transformer predictions

categories.name: checkpoint_selection
categories.definition: Selecting which saved model checkpoint(s) to use for inference, including epoch selection, fold-specific checkpoints, and quality filtering of checkpoints.

categories.name: backbone_swap
categories.definition: Replacing the core pretrained model architecture or backbone variant used within a single model component.

categories.name: model_architecture_design
categories.definition: Designing or modifying the structure of a model's layers, heads, channels, or capacity (width, depth, attention blocks) beyond simply swapping a pretrained backbone.
examples: 1D CNN model capacity (width, depth, head size)
model head architecture alignment with checkpoint

categories.name: model_family_selection
categories.definition: Choosing or switching between fundamentally different model families or paradigms (e.g., GBDT vs transformer vs SVR) as the primary modeling approach.

categories.name: gbdt_hyperparameters
categories.definition: Tuning hyperparameters specific to gradient-boosted decision tree models such as depth, leaves, learning rate, regularization, and boosting rounds.
examples: L1/L2 regularization strength in gradient boosting

categories.name: learning_rate_and_training_schedule
categories.definition: Setting or adjusting the learning rate, number of training iterations, early stopping patience, or loss function for model training.
examples: focal loss with higher learning rate

categories.name: feature_engineering
categories.definition: Creating new input features from raw data, including aggregations, lag features, text statistics, date transformations, and custom domain-specific features.

categories.name: feature_selection
categories.definition: Choosing which features to include or exclude from the model input, including importance-based pruning, add-then-prune strategies, and feature toggle evaluation.
examples: feature selection via dropping low-importance features

categories.name: text_feature_extraction
categories.definition: Extracting features from text data using NLP techniques such as TF-IDF, embeddings, or handcrafted linguistic statistics.
examples: dense linguistic features on top of high-dimensional text features
Handcrafted text features for the GBDT component

categories.name: embedding_and_representation_extraction
categories.definition: Using pretrained model hidden states or embeddings as input features for downstream models, including consistency of embedding sources.
examples: Transformer hidden-state embeddings as tabular features

categories.name: input_modality_composition
categories.definition: Selecting or combining different input data modalities or branches (e.g., image, text, signal, tabular) fed into the model.
examples: additional input branch with alternative feature extraction from same modality

categories.name: signal_and_spectrogram_preprocessing
categories.definition: Processing raw signals (e.g., EEG) into spectrograms or applying domain-specific filtering, clipping, normalization, or cropping before model input.
examples: EEG signal filtering and spectrogram clipping/normalization
spectrogram preprocessing parameters and model architecture variant
spectrogram vertical crop and dataset slice bounds

categories.name: text_preprocessing
categories.definition: Cleaning, normalizing, or transforming raw text inputs before they are fed to a model, including tokenization alignment.

categories.name: image_resolution_and_augmentation
categories.definition: Setting input image resolution, matching it to model expectations, and configuring data augmentation strategies.
examples: Input image resolution and matching checkpoint
train/val split ratio and color augmentation diversity

categories.name: data_cleaning_and_filtering
categories.definition: Filtering, imputing, or removing problematic data points such as outliers, NaNs, or high-NA columns before training or inference.
examples: NaN handling strategy for derived aggregation features
drop high-NA raw columns before feature engineering

categories.name: target_transformation
categories.definition: Transforming the prediction target or output values, including centering, scaling, or changing the output formulation.
examples: number of output bins in classification head

categories.name: cv_strategy
categories.definition: Designing the cross-validation splitting strategy, fold construction, group assignments, and fold count.
examples: CV split strategy and fold index construction
KMeans clustering on text features for CV group assignment

categories.name: postprocessing_rounding_and_thresholding
categories.definition: Applying discretization, binning, rounding, or thresholding to model predictions as a post-processing step.

categories.name: postprocessing_calibration_and_scaling
categories.definition: Calibrating, normalizing, rescaling, or power-transforming prediction probabilities or values after model output.

categories.name: postprocessing_strategy_selection
categories.definition: Choosing between qualitatively different post-processing approaches or toggling post-processing on/off.
examples: strategy pivot to qualitatively different post-processing

categories.name: custom_postprocessing_logic
categories.definition: Implementing specialized or rule-based post-processing logic such as JIT-compiled ranking, confidence-based adjustments, or heuristic overrides.
examples: rule-based feature override for specific target columns

categories.name: stacking_and_meta_learning
categories.definition: Building stacking ensembles or meta-learners that use base model predictions as features, including meta-learner architecture and hyperparameter choices.
examples: per-fold ridge ensembler over diverse transformer predictions

categories.name: multi_seed_averaging
categories.definition: Running the same model with multiple random seeds and averaging predictions to reduce variance.
examples: controlling for randomness during manual sweeps

categories.name: test_time_augmentation
categories.definition: Applying augmentations or perturbations at inference time and averaging the resulting predictions.
examples: test-time augmentation with shifted temporal crops

categories.name: inference_pipeline_architecture
categories.definition: Structuring or refactoring the overall inference pipeline, including model loading, routing, serialization, and softmax placement.
examples: custom inference script with explicit model loading and prediction

categories.name: memory_and_compute_optimization
categories.definition: Managing GPU/CPU memory, batch sizes, garbage collection, sequential load-free loops, and compute backends during inference.
examples: explicit garbage collection during inference loops

categories.name: offline_training_and_precomputation
categories.definition: Training models or computing features offline and loading precomputed artifacts at inference time.
examples: Offline training with pretrained model loading
retrain/improve external GBDT fold models offline

categories.name: bug_fix_and_code_correctness
categories.definition: Identifying and fixing bugs, syntax errors, indentation issues, import failures, or incorrect variable references in the pipeline code.
examples: Immediate indentation/scope fix after large additions

categories.name: pipeline_debugging
categories.definition: Systematically diagnosing and resolving integration issues, infrastructure failures, or unexpected behaviors in the pipeline before evaluation.

categories.name: pipeline_simplification_and_refactoring
categories.definition: Restructuring, simplifying, or cleaning up pipeline code for clarity, maintainability, or correctness without changing the modeling approach.
examples: Code correctness audit and pipeline simplification

categories.name: dependency_and_environment_management
categories.definition: Managing library imports, package compatibility, device placement, and runtime infrastructure.

categories.name: ablation_and_component_isolation
categories.definition: Testing the contribution of individual components by removing, reverting, or isolating them to understand their effect.

categories.name: revert_and_rollback
categories.definition: Reverting changes that caused regressions or rolling back to a known-good configuration as a recovery strategy.

categories.name: experiment_batching_and_isolation
categories.definition: Deciding whether to bundle multiple changes into one submission or isolate them, and managing change granularity.
examples: Batch multiple orthogonal improvements into one submission
isolating sources of improvement by changing one dimension at a time

categories.name: experiment_scheduling_and_stopping
categories.definition: Deciding what to try next, when to stop a line of investigation, when to pivot to a different lever, and managing experiment prioritization.
examples: stopping criterion for a sweep of worsening variants

categories.name: submission_strategy_and_variance_estimation
categories.definition: Managing submission budget, timing, re-submissions for variance estimation, and interpreting noisy leaderboard signals.

categories.name: local_validation_and_gating
categories.definition: Using local CV or holdout evaluation to gate submissions, validate components, or serve as a fast proxy before leaderboard evaluation.
examples: offline CV-based validation of ensemble components
